sense: a boat or a ship; a rocket

terms.gloss: launch (a ship), draw down into the water
evidence: Caes. BG 5.2.2: quīn paucīs diēbus dēdūcī possint
Verg. A. 4.398: nāvēs lītore dēdūcunt (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The seaman’s word: to draw a ship down from the stocks or the beach into the sea (Lewis & Short); the opposite is subdūcere, to haul it up. Its other common senses are to lead away, to escort (a bride to her husband’s house), to found a colony, and to deduct a sum.

terms.grammar: verb phrase: ēmittō, ēmittere, ēmīsī, ēmissum
evidence: M-O s.v. launch (a spacecraft), after Egger
terms.comment: Egger’s phrase, “to send up on high”; he also has in aethera ēmittere and in ināne īnfīnītum ēmittere (M-O). Ēmittere is classically to send out, let go, and of weapons to shoot (Lewis & Short).

phrases.english: and the winches drag the dry hulls down to the sea

phrases.latin: nāvēs … invēnit īnstrūctās neque multum abesse ab eō quīn paucīs diēbus dēdūcī possint
phrases.english: he found the ships fitted out and nearly ready to be launched in a few days

sources: Lewis & Short: deduco · Lewis & Short: emitto
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. launch (a spacecraft).
